name: Male Genital Pathology: Prostate, Testis, Penis and Scrotum

reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Peripheral hard PSA bone: prostate cancer
reference.pathophysiology: DHT hyperplasias transition while peripheral clones dedifferentiate into Gleason patterns metastasising osteoblastically; isochromosome 12p drives germ cells that AFP or hCG betray, and bell clapper mobility twists spermatic cords ischaemically.
additionalDifferentials: BPH versus cancer by zone and Gleason
Seminoma versus nonseminoma by markers and radio response
Torsion versus epididymitis by onset and Prehn
additionalInvestigations: PSA with rectal exam and MRI fusion biopsy in nodules
Testicular ultrasound with AFP, hCG and LDH in masses
Doppler in sudden scrotal pain within hours
